final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position by reinterpreting the same record. That narrower framing is directionally more accurate, but it still leaves the key compliance predicate unresolved. The admissible evidence supports that aggregate readiness currently passes and rehearsal was clean, but it also shows a material named-use-case weakness in medical device support and a policy requiring that such weaknesses be disclosed in current release documentation unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation before launch. The Actor expressly concedes that the record does not show current disclosure language and does not include approved mitigation or risk acceptance. That matters because a caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat describes a bounded condition within an otherwise satisfied compliance state; here, the caveat is itself an unsatisfied policy requirement. So the record supports only a conditional path to future compliance, not compliant certification on the present evidence.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card already discloses the medical-device-support limitation for the named launch use case.
No approved pre-launch mitigation or risk acceptance covers the subgroup regression.
The policy predicate is unresolved: disclosure or approved mitigation must exist before certification may proceed.
Prior family approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and cannot substitute for current documentation or reviewed acceptance.
